source: coral-xyz/multisig programs/multisig/src/lib.rs (master, Apache-2.0), built with Anchor 0.31.1: bench/real/o_multisig
about: Open-source program, unmodified logic: the clean build is expected to have no finding; each variant removes exactly one validation and expects one of its rules at its instruction. Scored for rules only.

why.multisig: zero + signer: a fresh program-owned account whose discriminator is still zero (no re-initialization) and whose keypair signs (nobody can front-run the initialization of an account someone else allocated). Permissionless by design: anyone may create a multisig with any owners; threshold in 1..=owners.len() and unique owners are required.

why.transaction: zero + signer: fresh, never initialized, keypair signs.
why.proposer: Signer, and the handler requires proposer.key in multisig.owners (InvalidOwner): only an owner can propose and its own approval is recorded.

why.multisig: Account<Multisig>; constraint multisig.owner_set_seqno == transaction.owner_set_seqno (approvals of a replaced owner set are void).
why.transaction: Account<Transaction>, mut, has_one = multisig: the transaction belongs to this multisig.
why.owner: Signer, and the handler looks it up in multisig.owners (InvalidOwner): only an owner can set its own approval bit.

why.multisig_signer: Signer with seeds = [multisig.key()], bump = multisig.nonce: only this multisig's PDA can sign, i.e. only execute_transaction of an approved transaction (invoke_signed) reaches it.
Signer + seeds [multisig.key()] / bump multisig.nonce: the multisig's own PDA (via execute_transaction). Unique, non-empty owners; seqno bumped (pending approvals invalidated).
Signer + seeds [multisig.key()] / bump multisig.nonce (the multisig's PDA). 0 < threshold <= owners.len().

why.multisig: Account<Multisig>; seqno equal to the transaction's.
why.multisig_signer: seeds [multisig.key()] / bump multisig.nonce: only used to mark the PDA's account metas as signer; the invoke_signed seeds are rebuilt from multisig.key() and nonce, so the PDA that signs is this multisig's.
why.transaction: Account<Transaction>, mut, has_one = multisig; did_execute checked and set; approvals >= multisig.threshold. The CPI target (transaction.program_id) and its accounts (remaining accounts) are arbitrary by design: they are what the owners approved.

create_tx_no_signer.impact: Anyone can create a transaction pre-approved by any owner (the handler only checks that the key is in owners): each such transaction counts one approval its owner never gave, so a threshold-1 multisig executes anything anyone proposes and a threshold-2 one needs a single real approval. Nothing else requires the proposer's signature (no CPI, no other constraint on it).

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: proposer.signer; in the variant only: proposer.count

approve_no_signer.impact: Anyone can set the approval bit of every owner (passing their keys unsigned), reach the threshold alone and then run execute_transaction: full control of the multisig PDA. The owner-list lookup is the only other check and does not involve a signature.

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: owner.signer; in the variant only: owner.count

approve_no_has_one.impact: An owner of any multisig (e.g. one the attacker creates with owners [A1..An] he controls, same seqno) passes it with a victim multisig's transaction: the owner index is looked up in the attacker's multisig and the victim transaction's approval bits get set, reaching its threshold. The seqno constraint only compares two counters the attacker can match (new multisigs start at 0).

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: multisig.raw, transaction.has_one, has_one multisig.key ~ transaction.multisig

auth_no_signer.impact: The PDA's address is public: anyone passes it unsigned and replaces the owners of any multisig (set_owners; also change_threshold / set_owners_and_change_threshold, same Auth struct): takeover. The seeds constraint only checks the address, not a signature.

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: multisig_signer.signer; in the variant only: multisig_signer.count

auth_no_seeds.impact: Any signer (e.g. the attacker's wallet) is accepted as multisig_signer: anyone replaces the owners / threshold of any multisig. Nothing else relates the signer to the multisig.

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: multisig_signer.signer, multisig_signer.pda

exec_no_has_one.impact: A transaction fully approved in the attacker's own multisig (owners he controls, seqno matched) is executed with a victim multisig: invoke_signed signs with the victim's PDA (seeds from the multisig account passed), so the attacker's instruction drains whatever the victim PDA controls. did_execute and the threshold are read from accounts the attacker controls.

verified.analysis: found in the clean build only: multisig_signer.key, transaction.has_one, has_one multisig.key ~ transaction.multisig

discarded.reason: redundant: invoke_signed rebuilds the seeds from multisig.key() and multisig.nonce, so only this multisig's PDA ever signs; another key passed as multisig_signer only gets is_signer set in the account metas, which the runtime rejects unless that account really signed the outer transaction.

discarded.removal: CreateMultisig / CreateTransaction `signer` on the zero account
discarded.reason: not clearly exploitable: it guards against initializing an account allocated in an earlier transaction by someone else, but clients create and initialize in one transaction; kept out to avoid an uncertain label.
not an account validation of the listed kinds (a state counter); left out.
